items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: I don’t know if this is a generalization but the British writers seem to take great pride in details and making things absolutely correct, and I think of Chris Sheridan and the book on Count Basie that is unbelievable.

ctx.x: Well a little bit of that. I was very much helped by a marvelous man called Max Jones who was the premiere jazz critic of the “Melody Maker.” I got to know him early and we stayed firm friends right through to the end of his life. And he let me put, he started to publish little bits by me in the “Melody Maker” in the late 50s, and that was helpful. By then I’d started corresponding with one or two musicians and things like that. And you could kind of pass on a few newsy tidbits, and they would go into Max’s…

I don’t know if this is a generalization but the British writers seem to take great pride in details and making things absolutely correct, and I think of Chris Sheridan and the book on Count Basie that is unbelievable.
Sure. Do you know about the one he’s doing on Monk?
